Built 2026-11-26 16:39:56 PST by workflow/10_tomography/msh_flags/ (branch analysis/msh-analog-flags). Decision D-B108 (PI, 2026-11-26 16:09). Flag only: no event is deleted or moved. Private working page.

3,453rows in event_flags_v61.csv

Flag file: /wd1/mdenolle_data/reloc_v61/flags/event_flags_v61.csv, columns ID,event_flag: 3,453 rows = 3,322 non-empty v6.0 flags carried over unchanged + 131 analog_test_signal (0 of them also had a v6.0 flag, joined with ';'). Events not in the file have no flag. Candidates with all numbers: msh_analog_candidates.csv; every event in scope: work/events_scored.csv.

In scope: 25,950 events (7,576 in the Mount St Helens box, 25,648 with picks on a signal channel); 141 have a pick on the signal. Of the 358 box events deeper than 30 km (v6.0), 82 are flagged certain and 1 probable.

0. Findings and checks in short

  • The signal is wider than HSR, EDM and STD. The same pulse is injected at the same instant (to 0.1 s) on 25 UW analog channels: the 12 analog stations around the volcano, LCW, BOW, NLO, VG2, KMO, HBO and RNO (700-950 counts) and an inverted copy of about 3 counts on KOS, RVW, VLM, SSO, STW and RMW. No digital channel with data (CC, PB, TA) carries it. The rule uses all 25.
  • Timing. Two pulses every Wednesday, about 20 minutes apart, from 2011-05-18 to 2013-08-28, at 11:54-12:00 and 12:14-12:20 on the generator's clock, drifting 3.1 s earlier each week. The generator keeps the pre-2007 US daylight-saving rule, so on nine Wednesdays (March-early April, late October-early November) the pulses come at about 12:58 and 13:18 local time; a local-time window misses them. On four Wednesdays the plateau lasts from the first to the second pulse.
  • Result. 131 events certain (flagged), 5 probable, 3 mixed. 95 of the 131 are in the Mount St Helens box, and 82 of the 358 box events deeper than 30 km (v6.0) are flagged. Flagged events: v6.0 depth median 49 km (111 deeper than 30 km), every pick on signal channels for 127 of them (one late pick on a far station for the other 4), P picks on stations tens of km apart within 0.02-1.4 s of each other (no moveout). No flagged event has a ComCat match; their catalogue magnitudes are 0.9-3.2 (45 above 2.5), the size of the pulse, not of an earthquake.
  • Real earthquakes in the windows are not flagged. The three "mixed" events (27434, 63183, 66944) have 8-14 picks on stations without the signal, moveout of 3-7 s and no pick on a pulse edge (0 of 8 matched): real earthquakes that occurred within a minute or two of a pulse (example 27434 below). The guard keeps them out, and the waveform test agrees.
  • ComCat (ANSS 2010-2016, any event type, within 30 s and 150 km). None of the 131 certain, none of the 5 probable and none of the 68 waveform-only events (section 7b) is in ComCat. Baseline: 35 of 41 unflagged shallow (< 10 km) tier A-B box events with M ≥ 1.5 are in ComCat, and 5 of 5 with M ≥ 2.5; 45 flagged events have M above 2.5. All three mixed events are there (PNSN earthquakes uw60408441, uw60555031, uw60576537, 11-16 km deep): the guard kept real earthquakes out. Caution: 0 of 68 unflagged box events deeper than 30 km with M ≥ 2.5 (sample) and 0 of 17 at 10-30 km are in ComCat either: the deep population under the volcano holds other non-earthquakes this rule does not address.
  • Waveform test on controls. 400 random events with picks on signal channels outside the windows: 0 pass (0 of 2,338 picks on a pulse edge). 80 box events on Wednesdays 11:00-13:30 device time outside the windows: 2 pass, both outside the windows so not flagged: 8194 (2010-08-04 13:23 PDT, five picks on the end of a pulse: an irregular calibration the scan did not cover) and 19900 (two picks of one station, JUN, on a step). In the windows, 949 of 1,022 picks sit on a pulse edge.
  • Not flagged by the rule, but artificial by eye: the 5 probable events (11422, 11423, 17438, 24181, 33277: picks on a data gap after a pulse, on a short box without plateau, on glitches inside an irregular test sequence), and the 68 waveform-only events of the post-hoc sweep (pulses outside the scheduled windows, e.g. 2010-12-14, 2011-01-27, 2011-04-15, 2011-05-04, 2012-11-17, 2012-12-17, 2013-09-29/30). Both lists are for the PI's review (v6.2).

1. The rule (pre-registered)

Written to RULE.md at 2026-11-26 16:27:27 PST (time from date) and pushed in commit 7ae9b1a9 before any event was scored; md5 of the file now: 61b3513e6de308ba40da3071fcb1d3b7 (registered: 61b3513e6de308ba40da3071fcb1d3b7).

RULE.md
# Pre-registered rule: Mount St Helens analog test-signal events (catalog v6.1 event_flag)

Registered: 2026-11-26 16:27:27 PST (from `date` on the build machine), before any event was scored.
Decision: D-B108 (PI, 2026-11-26 16:09; workflow/10_tomography/DECISIONS.md on origin/tomo/tiles 7b6b9173).
Code: workflow/10_tomography/msh_flags/ (branch analysis/msh-analog-flags). Flag only: no event is deleted or moved.

## What was looked at before this rule was written (window and channel definition only)

1. Pick timing (maf_hist.py): picks of HSR, EDM, STD.UW per weekday and local hour against all other stations; Wednesday
   11:00-13:30 local in 1-min bins per year; picks per station in the Wednesday noon window against the same clock
   window on the other weekdays. Result: two Wednesday clusters near 11:56-12:00 and 12:16-12:20 local, 2011-2013 only;
   the excess is on about 13 UW analog stations around the volcano, not only HSR, EDM, STD.
2. Continuous data (maf_template.py, maf_scan.py): template of the pulse from 16 traces (2011-11-23 and 2012-05-02, two
   pulses each, HSR/EDM/STD/SHW). Scan of every day 2010-2016 at EDM.UW and every Wednesday at HSR, STD, SHW, ELK.UW,
   11:00-13:30 local. Result: two pulses every Wednesday from 2011-05-18 to 2013-08-28, onsets identical to 0.1 s on all
   channels (common mode), drifting -3.1 s per week; the generator keeps the pre-2007 US DST rule (nine Wednesdays
   with pulses one hour late in local time); on four Wednesdays the plateau lasts from the first to the second pulse;
   13 irregular common-mode pulses on other days or times (2010-2016).
3. Station screen (maf_screen.py): 24 reference pulses at every station with picks within 300 km of the summit.
4. The edge detector (maf_wave.py) was run on 11 hand-chosen times of the continuous data (pulse edges, a long plateau,
   a Tuesday control). No catalog event was classified, and no class counts were computed before this rule.

## Definitions

- **Signal channels S** (maf_screen.py; WORK/signal_stations.json): stations whose vertical channel carries the pulse
  (|cc| >= 0.9 and amplitude/noise >= 5 within 2 s of the reference onset at half or more of the 24 reference pulses
  with data). 25 UW analog stations: HSR SHW EDM STD JUN SOS FL2 CDF ELK TDL MTM LVP LCW BOW NLO VG2 KMO HBO RNO
  (pulse of 700-950 counts) and KOS RVW VLM SSO STW RMW (inverted copy of about 3 counts; RMW from one pulse only).
  No digital station (CC, PB, XD, ...) carries it. HSR, EDM, STD are the three channels named by the v5.1 review.
- **Device time**: UTC - 8 h, plus 1 h from the first Sunday of April 02:00 PST to the last Sunday of October 02:00 PDT
  (pre-2007 US DST rule of the pulse generator). Local time is America/Los_Angeles (PST/PDT, 2007+ rule).
- **Pulse windows W** (maf_calendar.py; WORK/windows.csv), in UTC:
  - weekly pulses, era 2011-05-18 .. 2013-08-28, every Wednesday, pulse 1 (device 11:50-12:05) and pulse 2 (device
    12:10-12:25): detected common-mode onset (two or more scanned stations within 2 s) -40 s .. +90 s; where a pulse was
    not detected, the onset predicted by linear interpolation in device time between the nearest detected Wednesdays,
    -120 s .. +150 s;
  - irregular pulses: common-mode detections outside those windows, onset -40 s .. +90 s.
- **Pick on the signal**: a pick (P or S) on a station of S whose time lies in W.

## Event rule

Scope: every catalog v6.0 event in the Mount St Helens box (46.05-46.30 N, 122.35-122.10 W; v6.0 epicentre, the v4
epicentre for events without a v6.0 hypocentre) and every event with at least one pick on a station of S.
Pick file: Cascadia_picks_catalog_v4.1tc.csv (pick_datetime).

For each event: n_tot = all picks, n_in = picks on the signal, share = n_in / n_tot, n_nonS = picks on stations not in S.

1. **Timing (T)**: n_in >= 3 and share >= 0.5.
2. **Waveform (WF)**: for up to 8 picks on the signal (P first, then by time), read pick - 45 s .. pick + 45 s of the
   station's vertical (pnwstore, record-header time base; raw counts, 10-Hz block means) and correlate the two edge
   templates (onset edge, the negative box masked; plateau end), either polarity. A pick is matched when an edge with
   |cc| >= 0.9 and |amplitude| / noise >= 5 lies at most 3 s after or 10 s before the pick
   (edge - 3 s <= pick <= edge + 10 s). n_wf = picks read with data, n_match = matched picks.
   WF holds when n_match >= 2 and n_match >= 0.5 n_wf.
3. **Real-earthquake guard (G)**: n_nonS <= 3 (an event with four or more picks on stations without the signal may be a
   real earthquake that happened during a pulse; it is not flagged).

Classes:
- **certain** = T and WF and G -> event_flag "analog_test_signal" in event_flags_v61.csv;
- **probable** = T and G, not WF (timing only; WF failed or no waveform) -> listed, not flagged;
- **mixed** = T, not G -> listed for review, not flagged;
- **none** = not T.

The flag file carries "certain" only. Every non-empty v6.0 event_flag is carried over unchanged; an event that already
has a flag and is "certain" gets the two joined with ';' (existing value first).

## Checks reported (no threshold is changed after scoring; any departure is reported as such)

- counts by class, by year, by window kind (weekly / irregular) and by box membership;
- depth of flagged events against unflagged events in the box;
- false-positive checks: (a) events with picks on the signal and 4 or more non-S picks (mixed) are listed and inspected;
  (b) WF run on control events without picks in W (a random sample of 400 events with >= 3 picks on S, and every box
  event on a Wednesday 11:00-13:30 device time outside W): the share of controls with WF true is the false-match rate;
  (c) flagged events with a ComCat match (comcat_id) or a magnitude above 2.5 are listed;
  (d) waveform examples of flagged events and of a real event in or next to a window.

2. The signal

A calibration-type pulse injected at once on the analog UW channels: a clipped negative box of 1.5 s, an exponential rise to a plateau of 700-950 counts, the plateau end 27.5 s after the onset and an exponential return. Two pulses every Wednesday, about 20 minutes apart. Template (median of 16 traces, plateau normalised; the negative box is masked in the correlation):

Raw traces of one Wednesday (2012-05-02): every analog station near the volcano, none of the digital ones

3. When: weekday and hour

Picks of HSR, EDM and STD.UW per weekday and local hour (left) and their share against all other stations' picks (right):

Wednesday 11:00-13:30 local in 1-minute bins, per year (orange: mean of the other weekdays at the same clock time):

Pulse calendar from the continuous data

Every day 2010-2016 at EDM.UW and every Wednesday at HSR, STD, SHW and ELK.UW, 11:00-13:30 local, scanned with the template. Weekly pulses from 2011-05-18 to 2013-08-28 (120 Wednesdays; pulse 1 detected on 115, pulse 2 on 111, the others predicted), drifting -3.1 s per week. The generator keeps the pre-2007 US daylight-saving rule: in the weeks between the 2007+ change date and the old one the pulses come one hour late in local time (2011-11-02, 2012-03-14, 2012-03-21, 2012-03-28, 2012-10-31, 2013-03-13, 2013-03-20, 2013-03-27, 2013-04-03). In device time the pulses stay at 11:54-12:00 and 12:14-12:20. 13 irregular common-mode pulses (other days or times) are windows too.

7b. Post-hoc sweep: pulse edges outside the windows (not part of the rule; no flag)

Events with no pick in the windows, 3 or more picks on signal channels and a P span of 1 s or less on them (68 listed): up to 4 picks each (one per station) tested with the same edge test; listed when 2 or more picks at 2 or more stations sit on a pulse edge. These are artificial pulses at times the weekly calendar and the noon scan do not cover (irregular calibrations). File: msh_analog_waveform_only.csv.
